services.desc: Art in public spaces, including murals, can serve as a vehicle for dialogue about history, describe relationships, and depict the resilience of the community in the hope to create equity, agency, and healing. Created between 2020-2023, Naranjo Morse explains: “This mural made of both acrylic and clay depicts compassionate Beings traveling and arriving at a point of enormous transformation which is expressed by brilliant light and form. Where they come from is remembered by what they carry. This project, began in the depth of Covid, desperate global migrations, the killing of Brianna Taylor and George Floyd and mass shootings. services.name: Docent Training
services.desc: The Wheelwright Museum of the American Indian has openings for museum docents! If you would like to be a volunteer docent, we will be accepting applications until February 9th for docent training this year. Complete an application, either online, by downloading the document below and emailing the completed application to info@wheelwright.org or in person, by downloading the document below and bringing a printed and completed copy to the museum, by February 9th. Applicants will be invited to an introductory Q&A at the museum on January 26th to meet museum staff, the current docents, and members of the Friends Council.
